content: I just now accidentally force pushed to master instead of my PR branch (due pressing the wrong key in magit). I pushed a revert commit and hope that I did not accidentally override anything (I fetched just before so I hope it should be fine). But overall, I think it would be great to protect the master branch such that one cannot directly push it. I think it would be good to enforce that all changes need to go through PRs. I think one can enable this in the Github repo settings, but I don't have access to them. Any thoughts on this?
Sure, good idea. I enabled protection so that all commits to master must go through a PR.
